Rashi on Berakhot 58b:10:1.hebrew: קפוף - עוף שקורין וולטו"ר, ויש לו לסתות ולחיים כאדם:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:10:1.english: Kippof - A bird called *voltor* [vulture], and it has jaws and cheeks like a human.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:11:1.hebrew: כוכבא דשביט - כוכב היורד כחץ ברקיע ממקום למקום, וארוך כשבט שהוא יורה, ונראה כמו שפותח רקיע:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:11:1.english: A comet - A star that descends like an arrow in the firmament from place to place, and is long like a staff as it shoots, and appears as though it opens the firmament.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:11:2.english: And we have a tradition that it does not pass Kesil - That it does not pass across the constellation of Kesil [Orion] when it is a shooting star.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:11:4.hebrew: רב הונא אמר - מאי זיקין? וילון הוא דמקרע, ומתחזי רקיע דרך הקריעה כרומח:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:11:4.english: Rav Huna said - [In answer to the question,] "What are zikin?" — it is Vilon that tears, and the firmament is seen through the tear like a spear.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:12:1.hebrew: כתיב עושה עש כסיל וכימה - דקדמיה ליה כסיל לכימה:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:12:1.english: It is written: “Who makes Ash, Kesil, and Kimah” - In that [Scripture] placed Kesil [Orion] before Kimah [the Pleiades].

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:12:2.english: How is this [reconciled]? - It teaches that both of them are equal.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:12:3.hebrew: שאלמלא חמה של כסיל וכו' - כסיל שולט בימות החמה, להכי אקדמיה קרא. כימה שולט בימות הגשמים, ולהכי אקדמיה קרא:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:12:3.english: That were it not for the heat of Orion, etc. - Orion dominates during the summer season; that is why the verse gave it precedence. Pleiades dominates during the rainy season; and that is why the verse gave it precedence.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:13:1.hebrew: עקרב - היינו כימה, וממזל טלה הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:13:1.english: Scorpion - That is Kimah, and it is of the constellation of Aries.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:13:2.english: The sting of the scorpion - The tail of the scorpion.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:13:3.hebrew: נהר דינור - מתשת כחו של עקרב:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:13:3.english: The River of Fire - It weakens the power of the scorpion.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:13:4.english: The chains of Kimah - The knots of Kimah.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:14:1.hebrew: כמאה ככבי - יש בין הכוכבים של כימה שהן כחה של כימה:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:14:1.english: About a hundred stars - There are [about a hundred stars] among the stars of Kimah that are the strength of Kimah.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:14:2.hebrew: אמרי לה דמכנפי - אותן שהן כחה של כימה, ואמרי לה דמבדרן:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:14:2.english: Some say that they are clustered - [Namely,] those [stars] that are the strength of Kima; and some say that they are dispersed.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:1.hebrew: יותא אמרי לה - דקיימא בזנב טלה, ואמרי לה דקיימא בריש עגלא:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:1.english: Yota; some say - That it stands in the tail of the Lamb [Aries], and some say that it stands in the head of the Calf [Taurus].

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:2.hebrew: רישא דעגלא - ראשו של עגל, והיינו מזל שור. והוא נמשך אחר מזל טלה — ראש השור סמוך לזנב טלה, שכן הסדר: טלה, שור, תאומים:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:2.english: The head of the calf - The head of a calf, and that is the constellation of Taurus. And it follows after the constellation of Aries — the head of the Bull is adjacent to the tail of the Ram, for such is the order: Aries, Taurus, Gemini.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:3.hebrew: ומסתברא כמאן דאמר זנב - היינו כוכבים העשויין כזנב, מדכתיב: ועיש על בניה תנחם:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:3.english: And it stands to reason in accordance with the one who said the tail - That is, stars that are shaped like a tail, as it is written: "And can you guide Ayish with her sons?"

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:4.hebrew: אלמא חסרה - והאי זנב מחזי כטרפא דטריף:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:15:4.english: Apparently it is lacking - And this tail appears like a torn leaf.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:1:1.hebrew: ברוך מציב גבול אלמנה - כגון בישוב בית שני:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:1:1.english: Blessed… Who establishes the border of the widow - Such as during the settlement of the Second Temple [era].

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:1:2.hebrew: אומר ברוך דיין האמת - דומיא דקטע, וקטע בתר דאתיליד הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:1:2.english: [One] recites: Blessed is the true Judge - [This is] similar to an amputee, and an amputee [became so] after he was born.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:3:1.hebrew: נפל ליה בתלא - שנפל לו ונעשה תל:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:3:1.english: It fell into a mound - That it collapsed and became a mound.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:4:1.hebrew: דיו לעבד שיהא כרבו - שהרי בית המקדש חרב, שהוא ביתו של הקב"ה:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:4:1.english: It is enough for a servant to be like his master - For the Holy Temple is destroyed, which is the house of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:6:1.hebrew: ככלי אובד - וסתם כלי לאחר י"ב חדש משתכח מן הלב, דיאוש בעלים לאחר י"ב חדש. בפרק אלו מציאות (בבא מציעא ד' כח.): מי שמצא כלי או שום מציאה חייב להכריז שלש רגלים, ואם נמצא אחר הסוכות, צריך להמתין ולהכריז בפסח ובעצרת ובחג — דהיינו י"ב חדש — ושוב אין צריך להכריז:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:6:1.english: Like a lost vessel - And an ordinary vessel is forgotten from the heart after twelve months, for the owner's despair [occurs] after twelve months. In the chapter 'Elu Metzi'ot' (Bava Metzia 28a): One who finds a vessel or any lost item is obligated to proclaim [it for] three pilgrimage Festivals. And if it was found after Sukkot, he must wait and proclaim [it] on Pesach, on Atzeret [Shavuot], and on the Festival [Sukkot] — which is twelve months — and thereafter he is no longer required to proclaim [it].

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:7:1.hebrew: אשר חלק ושהחיינו - דלאחר שלשים יום הוה:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:7:1.english: “Who has shared” and “Who has given us life” [Shehecheyanu] - For it was after thirty days [since they had last seen him].

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:7:2.hebrew: מחכמתו ליראיו - כרב חנינא, דחכים טפי:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:7:2.english: Of His wisdom to those who revere Him - Like Rav Ḥanina, who was exceedingly wise.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:1.english: Spotted people - Lentillous [in Old French, meaning freckled], [having spots] like lentils.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:2.english: A Cushite - [One who is] very black.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:3.english: A red-skinned person - [One who is] very red, rouge in Old French.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:4.english: An albino - [One who is] excessively white.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:5.hebrew: קפח - בטן גדול, מתוך עוביו נראית קומתו מקופחת. לשון אחר: קפח — ארוך הרבה, ופרצופו שמוט ובולט, דמכוער הוי:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:5.english: A kippeaḥ - [One with a] large belly; on account of his thickness, his stature appears truncated. Another explanation: A kippeaḥ [is] very tall, and his face is drooping and protruding, for he is unsightly.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:6.hebrew: הדרניקוס - רודא"ש. לשון אחר: פיו עקום:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:6.english: A hadranikos - [One who is] covered with warts [verruos in Old French]. Another explanation: His mouth is crooked.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:7.hebrew: אומר ברוך משנה את הבריות - דממעי אמן הוו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:7.english: [One] recites: Blessed… Who makes creatures different - For they were [so] from their mother's womb.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:8.hebrew: קטע - שנקטעו ידיו. הכא הוא דקטע משמע דידים — הוא משום דקתני תרתי: קטע וחגר. אבל היכא דקתני קטע לחוד, משמע דרגלים, כדתנן (שבת פ"ו ד' סה:): הקטע יוצא בקב שלו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:8.english: An amputee - [One] whose hands were severed. It is [only] here that kate'a implies [the] hands — this is because it taught two [categories]: kate'a and chiger [a lame person]. But wherever it teaches kate'a alone, it implies [the] legs, as we learned in a mishna (Shabbat, chapter 6, 65b): "An amputee may go out with his wooden leg."

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:9.hebrew: פתויי ראש - ששערו כנמטא, כל שערו דבוק זה בזה, פלטדי"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:8:9.english: A person with matted hair - [One] whose hair is like felt; all his hair is stuck together, feltrer [to mat] in Old French.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:9:1.hebrew: היכא דאיתרע ליה בתר דאתיליד - לאחר שנולד, נולדו בו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58b:9:1.english: Where [misfortune] befell him after he was born - After he was born, [the spots] developed in him.

Rashi on Berakhot 58b:9:2.english: Similar to an amputee - And an amputee is [one who became so] after he was born.

Tosafot on Berakhot 58b:11:1.hebrew: וילון הוא דמקרע ומחזי נהורא ברקיע - לפי הענין משמע דבא רב הונא לתרץ דלא עבר כסלא, ולא קאי אמתניתין לפרושי מאי זיקין; דהא רב אשי דבתריה קאי אשנויא דלא עבר כסלא, ודלא כפירוש רש"י:
Tosafot on Berakhot 58b:11:1.english: "It is Vilon that tears and reveals light in the firmament" - According to the context, it implies that Rav Huna came to resolve [the difficulty that a comet] does not pass Kesil [Orion], and he is not referring to the Mishnah to explain what zikin are; for Rav Ashi, who follows him, addresses the resolution of [the difficulty that] it does not pass Kesil — unlike the explanation of Rashi.

Tosafot on Berakhot 58b:6:1.hebrew: הרואה חבירו אחר שלשים יום אומר שהחיינו - אומר ר"י: דוקא חבירו החביב עליו, אבל בענין אחר — לא:
Tosafot on Berakhot 58b:6:1.english: "One who sees his friend after thirty days recites Shehecheyanu" - The Ri says: [This applies] specifically to his friend who is dear to him, but otherwise, not.

Tosafot on Berakhot 58b:6:2.hebrew: הרואה חבירו אחר שלשים יום אומר שהחיינו - אומר ר"י: דוקא חבירו החביב עליו, אבל בענין אחר — לא:
Tosafot on Berakhot 58b:6:2.english: "One who sees his friend after thirty days recites sheheḥeyanu" - The Ri says: Specifically [when it is] his friend who is dear to him, but otherwise, no.
